claims.text: Adding a small amount of Gd to a single-phase CoCrFeNi-based HEA will enhance its magnetocaloric effect.
The enhancement from Gd doping will occur through an increase in overall magnetic entropy change during magnetic-field cycling.
The initial CoCrFeNi-based HEA is a stable, single-phase solid solution.
A Gd concentration of 2–10 atomic percent is an appropriate minor-doping range for the HEA.
Arc melting followed by appropriate homogenization can retain a single-phase structure in the Gd-doped alloy.
The relevant magnetocaloric response should be measured near room temperature or near the base alloy's magnetic-ordering temperature.
The proposed structural mediator is a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure containing uniformly incorporated Gd atoms.
Gd has a high localized magnetic moment.
Gd moments incorporated into the HEA matrix can provide additional magnetic entropy.
The high configurational entropy of the HEA matrix helps stabilize the Gd-doped structure against phase separation.
Suppressing phase separation allows Gd magnetic moments to interact efficiently with the host magnetic lattice.
Interaction between Gd moments and the host magnetic lattice enhances the overall magnetocaloric response.
Gd doping is expected to increase magnetic entropy change by approximately 10–20% relative to the undoped HEA.
Magnetocaloric enhancement is expected only when Gd remains below approximately 10 atomic percent.
Higher Gd concentrations may cause phase segregation or secondary-phase formation.
Phase segregation or secondary phases could counteract the desired magnetic response.
